name: Anza RE, LLC (operating as Anza; branded Anza Renewables)
headquarters: Oakland, California, United States (legal and notice address 1440 Broadway, Suite 200 #1100; the California foreign-LLC record gives 1423 Broadway #1100; staff are remote across the United States)
employees: Not published. LinkedIn range '51-200 employees' (company-set) with 84 members listed (read 2026-10-04); PitchBook '86 total employees' (third-party estimate); the company's own pages name about 30 staff and four officers

ownership.notes: Energy Capital Partners-led consortium (ECP's Energy Transition Opportunities Fund, Angeleno Group and 'other investors') since the May 2023 separation from Borrego; terms never disclosed; management holds equity under 'an attractive equity program' (careers page); whether Borrego retained a stake is stated nowhere. Delaware LLC per state-registry mirrors (OpenCorporates DE file 7326972; the formation date is paywalled and the aggregator date of 2023-03-02/03 is unconfirmed); foreign-registered in California, Washington, New Hampshire and eleven other states from 3 May 2023

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Anza is the Oakland procurement-intelligence firm that turned Borrego's internal module-buying tools into four paid data subscriptions (Solar Pro, Anza Pulse, Energy Storage Pro, Energy Storage DG) and a fee-for-service procurement, commissioning and transformer-sourcing practice for developers, IPPs, EPCs, utilities and data-centre developers; its data claims rest on supplier participation it does not pay for — '40+ module, 20+ battery block and 50+ transformer suppliers' and 'more than 95% of the U.S. solar module and battery supply' (company statement, never audited) — and it earns on the procurement it advises, so it is an intermediary that publishes an index, not a neutral analyst. BACKGROUND. Strategy conceived in 2020 by Mike and Aaron Hall inside Borrego; platform live in 2021 (privacy policy effective 1 September 2021; LinkedIn 'Founded 2021'); formally launched as Borrego's procurement marketplace on 12 September 2022; separated on 17 May 2023 with funding from an Energy Capital Partners-led consortium (ECP's Energy Transition Opportunities Fund, Angeleno Group, others — 'terms of the transaction were not disclosed'); legal entity Anza RE, LLC, a Delaware LLC per state-registry mirrors, with California governing law in its terms. Commercial model, in the company's and third parties' words: buyers 'pay us for access to the data and technology and also the services' (CEO, Solar Builder, April 2024); 'approximately 1-2 cents per watt on projects, with utility-scale fees measured in tenths of a cent' (CEO, Clean Power Hour, September 2023); 'tiered subscription packages' with no published price list; Anza Pulse and Energy Storage DG are self-serve, card-billed, auto-renewing subscriptions with a 14-day Pulse trial. Scale as stated by the company (none audited): '100+ current subscribers'; '9.2+ GW of solar POs and 4.7+ GWh of energy storage POs' supported in five years (about-us, June 2026) against 'over 10 GW of solar & 8 GWh of BESS experience' on a page updated September 2026 and '8 GW of PV and 7 GWh of BESS purchase orders' in December 2025 — three figures for the same claim; '11 GWh' of BESS construction and commissioning support; 'over 5 GW of module procurement over the past 12 months' (September 2026). Collection gaps: revenue, subscription prices, the per-watt fee on storage, the transformer-service fee, headcount, Borrego's residual stake and any funding since 2023 are published nowhere; no data-centre developer or transformer client is named.
ecosystemRole: The corpus's ninth `advisor` and its first procurement-side one: where DNV and Sargent & Lundy sell the engineering judgment a lender relies on, Anza sells the market view a buyer needs before the purchase order — supplier-provided price, lead-time, FEOC, domestic-content and certification data on the modules, battery blocks, PCS and transformers that this corpus's suppliers make and its developers buy — and then runs the RFP, BAFO and pre-negotiated Supplier Purchase Agreement for a per-watt fee, warehouses the equipment, and manages BESS commissioning (GridStor's 220 MW / 440 MWh Texas plant; Aypa's 150 MW ERCOT battery). Category decision: `advisor`, not `supplier`. The subscriptions are software and data products sold on their own terms, but they are procurement intelligence of the kind SemiAnalysis sells to the same buyer function, not operating software a plant runs on; the only fee model either the company or a third party has described is buyer-paid procurement fees plus subscriptions, and neither has published the revenue split, so the record supports one category. Independence: its indices are built from quotes suppliers hand over in exchange for free market feedback and the chance to 'win more business' through Anza's procurements; trade press (Utility Dive, Forbes) nonetheless cites them beside Wood Mackenzie's as neutral market data. No covered dossier names Anza.

productsAndServices.name: Energy Storage Pro — utility-scale and high-volume DG battery data and analytics subscription
productsAndServices.category: Software and data subscription — energy storage
productsAndServices.description: A subscription database and modelling engine for battery energy storage procurement: supplier-provided FOB/DDP pricing, CapEx and OpEx 'for deliveries 3 years out, including system, block, & PCS pricing', 150-plus data fields across batteries, PCS and full configurations, 30-plus filters (Tier-1 status, PCS compatibility, country of origin, certification, FEOC tier, domestic-content eligibility), downloadable datasheets, UL 9540 certificates, single-line diagrams and cash-flow models, side-by-side comparison of up to four systems, and since March 2026 an automated scenario engine (duration, tariff severity, delivery timing, augmentation versus overbuild, supplier degradation curves) with confidential quote benchmarking.
highlights: Launched 13 May 2025 'across more than 20 battery suppliers, including fully domestic and non-Chinese options' with 'real-time access to more than 150 data fields'; the launch blog claimed pricing 'for more than 85% of U.S. BESS supply', restated as '95% of the U.S. battery market' on 3 March 2026 — the 85 percent figure still appears in a September 2026 blog ('pricing data from 85% of current suppliers') and Utility Dive (7 April 2026) reported '85% of energy storage market' in the same quarter the release said 95 percent. Company claims; no third party has tested either denominator.

3 March 2026: 'the first market-wide scenario intelligence engine purpose-built for utility-scale and DG battery energy storage system (BESS) development and procurement' — 'model duration scenarios, tariff severity outcomes, delivery timing shifts, and probability-weighted pricing assumptions', 'supplier-specific degradation curves', 'AC/DC augmentation or overbuild strategies', and 'Centralized Quote Benchmarking' against 'standardized data covering 95% of U.S. battery suppliers'; the companion blog claims 'compatibility checks in under a minute and the ability to model 10+ trade-off scenarios in under 30 minutes'.

FEOC and FCC compliance as a product (blog, 29 September 2026): six FEOC status tiers from 'Not Compliant' to 'Legal Opinion Available'; across tracked storage products '40% of products in the high FEOC risk categories (Self-Reported, Not Compliant) and 25% of products in the low-risk categories … with roughly 35% … Pending'; a filter for 'FCC inverter compliance status' and the 'MACR points a particular solution (or variant) contributes'; the company commits to re-filter when DOE's rules issue in December 2026.

Current page (September 2026): 'add custom systems and your own supplier quotes to instantly (and confidentially) benchmark your offering against 30+ BESS suppliers and 55+ different products'; 'AC-wrapped and self-integrated product options'; filters for IEEE 2800, NERC IBR and RTO interconnection standards; total lifecycle cost 'including preventative maintenance, warranties, capacity maintenance, and LTSA'.

Named users: GridBeyond (beta; quote cycles 'up to three weeks' replaced by platform configurations), MMR/SouthWestern Power Group (beta), Standard Solar ('We rely on the platform to rapidly validate various sizing and scope iterations, solidifying our Basis of Design in real time' — CJ Colavito), New Leaf Energy (ECP-owned sibling; 'validating Anza's energy storage software against our internal design tool'), EnerSmart Storage, Chaberton Energy.
productsAndServices.positioning: Positioned against 'hard-to-get, quickly outdated pricing, siloed non-standardized product and supplier data, expensive consultants, and manual processes' (CEO at launch) rather than against a named vendor; no third party names a competitor, and Utility Dive runs Anza's median capex beside Wood Mackenzie's deployment data as parallel sources. The differentiation claimed is direct-from-supplier pricing updated monthly or more often, not modelled indices.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct subscription sold through the company's sales team ('Schedule a Meeting' order forms); 'tiered subscription packages custom built to fit companies' unique needs'; no price list published; Market Insights (quarterly report plus four hours of custom analysis per quarter) bundled with platform subscriptions.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Re-filtering for DOE's bulk-power-system rules 'due by December 24, 2026' (blog, 29 September 2026); a new storage webinar series launched 31 August 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Solar Pro — module data, analytics and optimisation subscription (Anza Effective $/W®)
productsAndServices.category: Software and data subscription — solar modules
productsAndServices.description: A subscription platform covering '95% of the U.S. module supply' (company) across 40-plus suppliers and 280-plus modules: ten quarters of supplier-provided pricing and availability, a five-year monthly machine-learning price forecast, a 'Predicted Quote' negotiated-price range, NPV ranking of modules against project specifications by the registered Anza Effective $/W® metric, a domestic-content blending tool for the 10 percent ITC adder, FEOC compliance filtering with Material Assistance Cost Ratio calculation, Anza Risk Rating® and vetted PAN, LID and IAM files.
highlights: Launched as a standalone subscription on 14 August 2024 'with access to data and insights of more than 95% of the U.S. module supply' and 'over 110 solar products'; 'Anza will offer tiered subscription packages custom built to fit companies' unique needs'.

26 August 2025 (RE+): 'Predicted Quote' — 'estimates the final negotiated price range for every module on the platform, using real-world, anonymized customer quotes and Anza's supplier negotiation experience. Prices are shown as a 25th–75th percentile range'; 'Quarterly Pricing' — '10 quarters (2.5 years) of supplier-provided module pricing'; 'Five-Year Monthly Forecast' — 'machine learning models to predict module prices up to five years out', trained on 'a structured two-year dataset from 40+ suppliers, with 10,000+ verified platform price points' (technology page).
Accuracy claim (pricing-advantage page, September 2026): 'Our solar module platform prices are within $0.008/watt of final supplier price quotes since September 2025.' Company statement.

FEOC (blog, 20 April 2026): a compliance filter over '240+ modules', MACR calculated per module with the verification tier shown — 'legal opinion, third-party audit, or certificate, and at the module OEM, cell, and seller level'; 'Suppliers that are only self-reporting … are not qualified as FEOC-compliant on the Anza platform'.

Named users: New Leaf Energy (vetting time 'from approximately 6 hours … to just 1 hour'), Apex Clean Energy ('Manual calculations that used to take the APEX team four hours can be completed in 30 minutes'), ClearPath Energy ('$12MM … saved by blending domestic and imported modules' — company calculator page), Alluvial Power, Birch Creek Energy, Renewable Properties, Spreck Energy, Working Power.
productsAndServices.positioning: Against periodic survey-based indices: 'The solar market intelligence category has been defined for years by periodic reports and bottom-up, component-based module pricing produced from annual supplier surveys and raw material price indexes' (Pulse release, May 2026). The pitch is live supplier quotes and project-specific NPV ranking; Latitude Media once labelled the company 'a solar energy equipment supplier', which it is not.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct tiered subscription via order form; brochure 'Solar Subscription Packages' (December 2025) implies tiers by use-case — development, buying soon, between purchases; no tier names or prices published.
targetSegments: Investors and independent engineers (named in the 2024 launch)
productsAndServices.roadmap: No announced items beyond the continuous tariff and FEOC updates.

productsAndServices.name: Anza Pulse — on-demand solar module market-intelligence subscription
productsAndServices.category: Software and data subscription — solar market intelligence
productsAndServices.description: A standalone, self-serve subscription 'built specifically for the work that happens between procurement cycles': live module pricing from 40 suppliers and 'over 1000 monthly price quotes, refreshed continuously and segmented by Tier 1, FEOC, domestic content', a Policy & Trade Navigator, a vetted supplier directory with contacts, and exportable bid snapshots; card-billed, auto-renewing, 14-day free trial.
highlights: Launched 27 May 2026 (covered as 'Solar Pulse' by Renewable Energy Magazine on 1 June and as 'Anza Pulse' by pv magazine India on 23 June — the brand settled within the month); CEO: 'We give you the data equivalent to running a fresh RFP across every supplier, every day of the year.'

Product page: '95% of U.S. module market covered / 40 suppliers tracked'; pre-built segments 'U.S. Assembly, Domestic Cells, Domestic Lite, FEOC-Compliant Cells, and Non-Domestic Modules'; 'Pricing reflects Anza supplier-provided platform pricing, shortlist and BAFO supplier quotes, and our price forecast logic'.

Terms (May 2026): subscriptions 'shall automatically renew … unless … cancel at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration'; 'ANZA DOES NOT PROVIDE REFUNDS OR CREDITS'; liability capped at fees paid in the prior six months; prices posted in-app, not on the public site.

Pulse data is the source of the free biweekly 'Pricing & Strategy Insights' and of the company's public tariff commentary — for example the Section 232 repricing data of 22 September 2026 (imported-module median $0.27/W to $0.38/W for delivery after 4 December).

Customer quote: 'Going to Anza Pulse is like having access to a Bloomberg terminal' — Jon Gillis, US Clean Energy; ForeFront Power's Monica Carter: 'It puts always-current supplier pricing and policy intelligence in one place.'
productsAndServices.positioning: The company's own description — 'Anza Pulse is a data subscription, not software' — places it against quarterly reports and 'modelled averages' from survey publishers; Anza names none of them.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-serve online subscription (credit card, auto-renew, 14-day trial) under the Anza Pulse Terms of Service; 'complements Anza's Solar Pro offering'.
targetSegments: Sourcing and procurement teams between buying cycles

productsAndServices.name: Energy Storage DG — entry-level C&I and distributed-generation storage data subscription
productsAndServices.category: Software and data subscription — distributed storage
productsAndServices.description: A standalone 'entry-level subscription' for C&I and DG storage developers and EPCs: budgetary pricing for AC-integrated systems sized to the project with east- or west-coast delivery, a searchable product library with FEOC status, domestic-content, safety certification and commercial-wrap data, and downloadable UL 9540 / 9540A / NFPA 855 / FSS documentation packages for AHJ submission.
highlights: Launched 28 May 2026 to 'help C&I and distributed generation storage developers and EPCs access traditionally hard-to-get pricing and technical product data and documentation earlier in the project lifecycle'; 'a standalone subscription priced to reflect the deal sizes and project economics in this segment'.

Product page: 'No callbacks. No stale quotes. No expensive distributor markups'; 'Tier 1, Domestic, and FEOC labels at the supply-variant level'; CEC-list and 'UL 1741 SA/SB interconnection eligibility at a glance'.
Shares the self-serve, card-billed, auto-renewing Terms of Service with Anza Pulse.
No third-party coverage beyond a wire reprint; no named customer.
productsAndServices.positioning: Against distributor quotes and callbacks in a segment the company says lacks data; the only competitor reference is 'expensive distributor markups'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-serve online subscription (card-billed); the entry point to the storage platform below Energy Storage Pro.

productsAndServices.name: Solar procurement advisory — 'Full Scope Procurement' and Pro Procure
productsAndServices.description: Fee-for-service module procurement for the buyer: supplier RFP and best-and-final-offer process, pre-negotiated Supplier Purchase Agreements and redlined terms with 'most U.S. OEMs', AD/CVD, FEOC and safe-harbor strategy, tariff-sharing clauses, vendor due diligence and third-party production inspection, with warehousing and order fulfilment as add-ons; the line that produces the company's GW-of-POs statistics.
highlights: Fee model as the company has described it to third parties: 'approximately 1-2 cents per watt on projects, with utility-scale fees measured in tenths of a cent' (CEO, Clean Power Hour, 22 September 2023); 'We sign a contract with the buyer, and the buyer pays us for access to the data and technology and also the services that we wrap the whole thing in' (CEO, Solar Builder, 3 April 2024); Solar Builder's note that Anza 'is not a distributor or middleman, though it has done some brokerage work but is moving out of that business'. No fee schedule is published.

Volume, in the company's own successive statements: '1.9 GW of module sales to date' (May 2023); 'more than 8.4 GW of cumulative solar procurements' (September 2025); 'over 8 GW of PV and 7 GWh of BESS purchase orders in the past five years' (December 2025); '9.2+ GW of solar POs and 4.7+ GWH of energy storage POs' (about-us, June 2026); 'Over 10 GW of Solar & 8 GWh of BESS Experience' (September 2026) — the BESS figure runs 4.7 / 7 / 8 GWh across pages of different vintage and no page reconciles them.

2025 safe-harbor season: 'over two gigawatts (GW) of solar modules in 2025, surpassing the total 2024 volume in just eight months'; 'Between June and August, Anza helped 15 customers … with 11 different solar module manufacturers, totaling over 1.2 GW' (release, 8 September 2025) — restated in September 2026 as '11 clients secure 1.1 GW of modules under Safe Harbor in two months'; 'over 5 GW of module procurement over the past 12 months' (22 September 2026).

Case studies the company publishes: NewSun Energy ('saving millions' on AD/CVD exposure, November 2024); Pacifico Power ('$0.04/watt' saving, '19% below our most recent quote', 17 MW, July 2025); 'a 200 MW replacement contract at $0.23/W covering approximately $10M of the tariff exposure' (blog, June 2025); Nofar USA ('Within 72 hours, we secured capacity with two top-tier suppliers'); Renewable Properties' 96 MW of VSUN and BYD modules in five deals (2022, under Borrego).

PV Module Warranty Insurance add-on 'offered through a third-party insurance provider … AA- S&P rated international company' (January 2023), still referenced as a project-level option in November 2025.
productsAndServices.positioning: Sold as faster and cheaper than an in-house RFP ('What takes customers 3 weeks becomes a 30-minute exercise' is the transformer-service wording; the solar line claims 'Anza helped five companies go from module selection to PO for 1.5 GW in less than 4 weeks'). The structural question no outlet has asked: the same firm publishes the price index and earns per watt on the procurement rush its commentary describes.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct advisory engagement under a buyer contract; per-watt and service fees (company and podcast statements); brochures 'Full Scope Procurement' and 'Solar Subscription Packages' (December 2025).

productsAndServices.name: Energy storage services — development, procurement and contracting, construction and commissioning, warehousing
productsAndServices.description: Four storage service lines: BESS Development Support (EPC selection, capacity feasibility, sizing and cost modelling, RFP responses, site layouts); BESS Procurement & Contracting Support (supplier RFP, BAFO shortlist, letter of exclusivity, BESA, MSA and LTSA negotiation support, technical exhibits); BESS Construction & Commissioning Execution Support (UL 9540 field-evaluation documentation, FIT and FAT witnessing, RFI support, OEM parameter review, on-site commissioning management, owner's-representative work); and Storage Warehousing & Logistics / Order Fulfillment (track-and-trace, customs documents, state-of-charge maintenance, warranty management, third-party inspections).
highlights: Scale claims: 'Over 19 GWh of Proven Expertise … 8 GWh of procurement support and 11 GWh of construction & commissioning support over the last 3 years' (services page, September 2026); the December 2025 brochure says '9 GWh of procurement support and 10.4 GWh of construction & commissioning support'; a blog of 31 August 2026 says 'more than 8 GWh of storage projects over the past year … across nearly 100 deployments'. Company statements.

Flagship case study (1 May 2026): GridStor's Texas plant, '220 MW/440MWh (68 inverter skids, 204 battery units)' — Anza as 'Commissioning Management, Technical Integration, Owner's Representative'; 'completed hot commissioning and ERCOT testing for the 220 MW facility in just two months'; 'award of a subsequent project in which Anza will provide full-scope commissioning and engineering support for GridStor's next major deployment'.
Aypa Power testimonial: 'Anza provided Aypa essential procurement and commissioning services for our 150 MW AC battery project in ERCOT' — Drew Silverman, VP Pre-Construction and Procurement.

Procurement stories: a 16 MWh Renewable Properties OEM pivot 'within four weeks' (September 2025); '18 MWh of storage in just seven days … We are now supporting that customer with another 100 MWh'; Alpha Omega Power's 'contract covering over 60 exhibits … in just two weeks—a process that typically takes two months'; an earlier page claims '$29/kWh' saved 'via a competitive shortlist process with three Tier-1 vendors'.

The company's own boundary: 'We're not an EPC or an independent engineer. But … for companies who are buying a DC block, we will help with commissioning, and contract supervision' (CEO, Troutman Pepper podcast, recorded 25 October 2024); warehousing priced in one public example at 'Add in warehousing service for 1 cent' per watt (September 2026).
productsAndServices.positioning: Sits between the owner and the OEM/EPC on self-integrated DC-block builds — the configuration the company says its data favours against 'fully integrated AC block solutions, Tesla maybe being … the most well-packaged' — without taking engineer-of-record or EPC risk.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct service engagements (owner's-representative, commissioning-management and procurement-support contracts); 'Energy Storage Services' brochure (December 2025).
productsAndServices.roadmap: A follow-on GridStor engagement for 'full-scope commissioning and engineering support' on its 'next major deployment' (May 2026; no size or date given).

productsAndServices.name: Transformer Procurement Service — MV/HV transformers and HV breakers
productsAndServices.description: A sourcing service launched 16 December 2025 under Felicity Lunden (ex-Quanta Infrastructure Solutions Group) 'for developers, IPPs, EPCs, utilities, and data center developers': market-wide supplier comparison across '50+ suppliers' of medium- and high-voltage transformers and HV breakers, lead-time and quote-response metrics, specification and quote reviews, supply-chain origin and tariff exposure, pre-negotiated Supplier Purchase Agreements, and ITC safe-harbor support. Sold as a service; there is no transformer data subscription.
highlights: Launch framing (release, 16 December 2025): 'medium voltage 9 weeks to 1 year and high voltage 2-4 years' lead times; 'massive price variances with wildly different quotes for identical specifications'; 'a network of 45+ MV/HV suppliers' — the page now says '50+' and 'MV transformer lead times (20 weeks to 1 year)'.

Claimed effect: 'creating a vendor contact list for an RFP … becomes a 30-minute exercise rather than many weeks'; pre-negotiated SPAs 'saving customers an estimated 2–6 months'; safe-harbor components 'seeing lead times of 18-20 weeks'.

Lunden 'brings over a decade of experience and a proven track record of more than 65 substation procurements across the U.S.' (release); earlier roles at Quanta Infrastructure Solutions Group, Wanzek Construction and Blattner Energy (webinar bio).

Traction: Transformers Magazine covered the January 2026 webinar; pv magazine USA's May 2026 transformer-market feature (Wood Mackenzie, Burns & McDonnell, Hitachi Energy, Siemens) did not cite Anza; no transformer client is named on any page.
productsAndServices.positioning: A procurement channel into the grid-equipment segment this corpus tracks (Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, ABB, Mitsubishi Electric), pitched on transparency over a bottleneck the company describes with the same lead-time figures the OEMs' own customers report; it names no OEM.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct service engagement; brochure 'Find MV/HV Transformer and HV Breaker suppliers' (January 2026); surplus units also listed on the Anza Exchange marketplace.
productsAndServices.roadmap: None announced beyond the Anza Exchange alpha for surplus transformers.

productsAndServices.name: Anza Exchange — alpha marketplace for surplus transformers, HV breakers and modules; Market Insights and free tools
productsAndServices.description: Anza Exchange (exchange.anzarenewables.com) is an alpha B2B marketplace 'to list & purchase new surplus transformers and solar modules' (homepage, March 2026), the remnant of the 2022 marketplace model. Market Insights — a quarterly report on policy, trade, supply chain, roadmaps, pricing and contract terms plus 'four hours custom analysis per quarter' — is bundled with subscriptions. Free lead-generation content: biweekly module and quarterly BESS pricing snapshots, a quarterly domestic-content report, three calculators (domestic content to IRS Notice 2025-08, Section 232 blending, Pulse ROI), webinars and case studies.
highlights: Anza Exchange has no press release, fee model or third-party coverage; its own page calls it 'the B2B marketplace for renewable energy equipment' for 'power transformers, HV breakers, and solar modules'.

The free quarterly series is what the trade press quotes: Q2 2025 'the sharpest single jump in battery energy storage prices since 2021' (DG 4-hour AC '+68%' January to May 2025); Q1 2026 utility-scale self-integrated '$145/kWh (down 5.8% from November's $154/kWh)'; module median '$0.28/W' (Q1 2026); US-assembled modules '$0.30/W' (July 2026); imported modules '$0.27/W' to '$0.38/W' after the Section 232 proclamation (September 2026). Three outlets printed three different 'February 2026 utility-scale' figures ($145, $158, $178 per kWh) for differently defined systems — quote with the system definition attached.

Market Insights content: 'AD/CVD cases, the latest on IEEPA tariffs, ITC beyond 2025, safe harbor deadlines … Current pricing and key contract terms from fully negotiated contracts, including available fixed price contracts and excess inventory'.

Two-sided mechanics (pricing-advantage page): 'Our team meets with all Anza platform suppliers every month … Suppliers update pricing to stay competitive, move up our ranking table, and win more business'; suppliers 'gain access to the U.S. market and real-time feedback' and 'Your Products Available to 80+ Subscribers with GWs & GWhs of Annual Demand'.
productsAndServices.positioning: The free series is the firm's public voice and the reason trade press cites it as a market tracker; the Exchange is an alpha with no disclosed traction.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Exchange: marketplace (fee model unpublished). Market Insights: bundled with platform subscriptions. Free tools: form-gated lead generation.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Exchange described as an 'alpha launch' (March 2026); no general-availability date.

recentDevelopments.read: The free price series is the firm's megaphone — and the rush it describes is the procurement it is paid per watt to run.

Anza's own release of 17 May 2023: 'An Energy Capital Partners led consortium of investors that included the ECP's–Energy Transition Opportunities Fund, Angeleno Group, and other investors provided funding to the company. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.' ECP partner Andrew Gilbert: 'As a leading investor in renewables, we frequently see the challenges developers, IPPs, and EPCs face in procuring major materials for their projects.'

ECP had bought Borrego's development business a year earlier (now New Leaf Energy), so the sponsor owns both halves of the former Borrego — the developer that buys equipment and the platform that prices it — and New Leaf is an Anza customer. Mergr and PitchBook describe the 2023 transaction as an acquisition; no stake percentage, Borrego residual or later round has been published, and ECP's Energy Transition Opportunities Fund is 'closed' with Anza as its most recent deal (PitchBook) — a 2023-vintage holding with an exit window ahead.

policyExposure.exposure: Anza's central 2026 product theme rather than a liability: it sells the compliance layer. Solar: a FEOC filter over '240+ modules' with the Material Assistance Cost Ratio calculated per module and the verification tier shown ('legal opinion, third-party audit, or certificate, and at the module OEM, cell, and seller level'); 'Suppliers that are only self-reporting … are not qualified as FEOC-compliant on the Anza platform.' Storage: six status tiers; across tracked products '40% … high FEOC risk … 25% … low-risk … roughly 35% … Pending' (September 2026). Utility Dive (April 2026): 79 storage products, 51% high or highest risk. Thresholds as Anza states them: solar MACR '40% non-PFE threshold [2026] … rises to 45% in 2027'; storage 'at least 55% … for a 2026 construction start, rising to 60% in 2027 and reaching 75% for projects beginning in 2030'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company-stated: documentation 'requested directly from suppliers'; a '60 point questionnaire' for FEOC risk ratings (CEO, October 2025); contract-review services for FEOC carve-outs.

policyExposure.exposure: The 6 August 2026 proclamation (effective 4 December 2026) set minimum import prices Anza publishes as '$21/kg poly, $100/kg ingots/wafers, $0.22/W cells, $0.38/W modules + 15% ad valorem'. Anza's platform data a month later: '55% of active suppliers' repriced, imported-module median '$0.27/W → $0.38/W' for post-deadline delivery, like-for-like quotes '+15%'. The firm's procurement volume is the exposure: tariff deadlines drive buying rushes it is paid per watt to execute, and 'over 5 GW of module procurement over the past 12 months' is the result.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company recommendations to clients: buy in-country inventory, lock domestic content, import before 4 December only with supplier tariff indemnity, 'consider First Solar'; a Section 232 blending calculator (21 August 2026).

policyExposure.exposure: The FCC's inverter Covered List (28 July 2026) and Executive Order 14421 (26 August 2026) reach the PCS and transformers Anza prices. Anza 'tracks equipment authorization status and covered-entity exposure at the supplier and product level', distinguishes 'Exempt systems (i.e., domestically produced) and those with Supplier Declaration of Conformity (SDoC)', and filters on 'FCC inverter compliance status'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Commitment to re-filter when DOE issues its rules 'due by December 24, 2026'.

policyExposure.exposure: The platform computes IRS domestic-content eligibility points and ITC value, blends domestic and imported modules for the 10 percent adder (ClearPath Energy '$12MM' saved, company figure), and the advisory practice sells safe-harbor execution — 'over 2 GW of solar modules in 2025' ahead of the 2 September 2025 deadline, with the OBBBA timeline ('begin construction by July 4, 2026, or be placed in service by Dec. 31, 2027') as the next clock. Two public calculators built to IRS Notice 2025-08 (thresholds 40%–60% for 2024–2028).
policyExposure.mitigation: None needed — the regime is demand.

policyExposure.exposure: Anza Risk Rating® fields assess 'FEOC compliance, tariffs, UFLPA, AD/CVD, and counterparty risk'; its commentary covers the Southeast Asia case ('Trina Solar Thailand, Canadian Solar, Runergy, Boviet Solar Technology, JA Solar Vietnam, and Jinko Solar Vietnam, receiving cash deposit rates between 50% and 80%'), Solar IV (India, Indonesia, Laos; preliminary CVD 23 February 2026, AD 27 March 2026) and active-anode-material duties ('$8–$15/kWh at the block level'). Case study: NewSun Energy 'saving millions' on AD/CVD exposure (November 2024).
policyExposure.mitigation: Tariff-sharing clauses in pre-negotiated SPAs — a '200 MW replacement contract at $0.23/W covering approximately $10M of the tariff exposure' (June 2025).

financials.commentary: Anza is private and publishes no financial statements. Every figure above is a company statement of volume, usage or subscriber count, dated to the page or release that carried it; where two company pages give two numbers for the same claim both are stated. No third-party revenue or valuation estimate is used. The structural facts a reader can rely on: buyer-paid per-watt procurement fees and tiered subscriptions are the only disclosed revenue mechanisms; suppliers pay nothing to be listed; the one financing is the undisclosed May 2023 ECP-led round.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Anza's business is a two-sided data exchange monetised on the buy side: suppliers hand over quotes, lead times and FEOC documentation in exchange for free market feedback and the chance to 'win more business' through Anza-run procurements, and buyers pay — per watt on procurements and by subscription for the data. Basis: the company's pricing-advantage page ('Our team meets with all Anza platform suppliers every month … Suppliers update pricing to stay competitive, move up our ranking table, and win more business'), the manufacturers page ('Your Products Available to 80+ Subscribers'), the CEO's own descriptions of the fee ('1-2 cents per watt'; buyers 'pay us for access to the data and technology and also the services') and the April 2025 episode in which 'every battery manufacturer tracked by Anza had paused price quotes' and the storage index went dark.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the firm is an intermediary that publishes an index, not a neutral analyst, and that the trade press has not yet priced that in. Basis: it earns on the volume of procurement its commentary describes (Section 232 'prices rising sharply' and 'over 5 GW … over the past 12 months' in the same release), it holds pre-negotiated agreements 'with most U.S. OEMs' whose prices it ranks, and no outlet read in this research has asked the question; Utility Dive and Forbes cite its medians beside Wood Mackenzie's. This is a characterisation of incentives, not an allegation of bias — no third party has found an error in the series.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the strategic pivot since 2024 is from marketplace to data subscription, and that the subscription business is still small relative to procurement services. Basis: four subscriptions launched in 26 months (Solar Pro, Energy Storage Pro, Anza Pulse, Energy Storage DG), the first two self-serve products in May 2026, Solar Builder's 2024 note that Anza 'has done some brokerage work but is moving out of that business', and the Anza Exchange marketplace surviving only as an alpha for surplus equipment; against that, every scale statistic the company publishes is a procurement figure (GW of POs) and the subscriber count is '100+'. The revenue split is undisclosed, so the weight is inferred.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the coverage claims ('95% of U.S. module supply', '95% of U.S. battery suppliers') are participation claims the company cannot audit and that have drifted upward with the product cycle. Basis: 90% at the 2022 launch, 'more than 85%' at the storage launch in May 2025, '95%' in March 2026, '85% of current suppliers' again in a September 2026 blog, and Utility Dive's '85%' in the quarter the release said 95%; no denominator has been defined in any outlet. The defensible figures are the supplier counts.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that FEOC and tariff compliance, not price discovery, is now the product's commercial edge. Basis: the 2026 release cadence — scenario engine with tariff-severity modelling (March), six-tier FEOC classification and MACR calculation (April–September), FCC Covered List and EO 14421 filters (September), two tariff calculators — and the company's own 'the compliance layer' framing; price data alone is replicable by a determined buyer, documentation verification at the OEM, cell and seller level is not.

6. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the Transformer Procurement Service and the stated 'data center developers' target are options, not yet businesses. Basis: no transformer client, volume or fee is named ten months after launch; pv magazine USA's May 2026 transformer feature did not cite Anza; no data-centre developer appears as a customer on any page, and the storage case studies (GridStor, Aypa) are grid-scale IPP projects. The service does give Anza a seat at the grid-equipment bottleneck this corpus's campuses wait on.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess that an ownership event is more likely than a growth round. Basis: ECP's Energy Transition Opportunities Fund is 'closed' with Anza as its most recent deal (15 May 2023, PitchBook); the sister Delaware entities ANZA RE BUYER, LLC and ANZA RE HOLDINGS, LLC suggest a sponsor holding structure; no round has been reported since 2023. Nothing has been announced; this is inference from vintage and structure.

Collection gaps: revenue, subscription prices, the storage take rate, the transformer fee, headcount, Borrego's residual stake, the Delaware formation date (aggregator-only), and the FY-by-FY procurement volumes behind the cumulative figures. Two founding dates (2021 platform; 2022 launch; 2023 separation) are each defensible for a different milestone and are stated as such.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — 4 December 2026, Section 232 effective date: whether Anza's post-deadline import median holds at $0.38/W (confirms the floor it published) or imports simply stop (confirms the procurement rush was pulled forward); by 24 December 2026, DOE's bulk-power rules: whether the platform's FCC/EO 14421 filters update within weeks (tests Judgment 5); the first named transformer or data-centre client (tests Judgment 6); a Q2/Q3 2026 storage pricing report with a defined denominator (tests Judgment 4); any funding, recapitalisation or sale announcement (tests Judgment 7); a supplier publicly withdrawing from the platform or disputing a ranking (tests Judgments 1–2).
